column1: # Standard English poetic elisions — the `elision` layer of quality/g2p.py.
# WHY THIS FILE HOLDS NO PHONES
# Every row names a CMUdict HEADWORD and a DECLARED OPERATION on that
# headword's pronunciation. Nothing here is a hand-written transcription, so
# the layer stays inside the rule the phonology already lives by: a fallback
# reading is admissible when every phone came out of a dictionary entry and the
# rule supplied only the change. A row whose basis is missing from the shipped
# cmudict.dict REFUSES rather than degrading (quality/test_g2p.py checks every
# row applies).
# SCOPE, AND THE THING THIS FILE IS NOT
# The closed class of standard English poetic contractions: aphesis
# ('gainst, 'neath, 'twixt, 'mongst), syncope (e'en, heav'n, pow'r, ev'ry) and
# the o'er / e'er pair. It is NOT a dialect table. Barnes's Dorset (zide,
# stwone, hwome) and Scots (awa, weel, e'e, o't) are refused by
# quality/g2p.py on the argument in its docstring: initial fricative voicing
# is a different phonology, not a different spelling, and reading it under a
# General American declaration would move the declaration's dialect coordinate
# without saying so (doctrine 1).
# COLUMNS
#   form      the elided surface form, lowercase, apostrophes folded to U+0027
#   full      the uncontracted form, for the reader
#   basis     a CMUdict headword; its FIRST listed pronunciation is the input
#   ops       comma-separated, applied left to right, indices into the basis
#             pronunciation BEFORE any op is applied:
#                =            identity (the basis is a homophone)
#                del:N        delete the phone at index N
#                sub:N=PHONE  replace the phone at index N
#                pre:PHONE    prepend a phone
#   note      why the basis is the basis
